ABSTRACT: A cobalt-catalyzed protocol for cascade coupling of
1,1-disubstituted allenes with aldehydes initiated by chemo-, regio-,
diastereo-, and enantioselective oxidative cyclization of allenes and
aldehydes followed by chemo-, regio-, and stereoselective addition
of the resulting allyl−cobalt intermediates to the second molecule

of aldehydes promoted by a chiral bisphosphine−cobalt complex is presented. Such processes represent an unprecedented reaction
pathway for cobalt catalysis that enables simultaneous and precise incorporation two molecules of aldehydes onto the more sterically
congested alkene of the allenes and construction of three stereogenic centers, delivering a range of enantioenriched 1,4-diols in up to
77% yield, >98:2 dr, and 98:2 er.

straightforward and modular approach for the construction
of chiral alcohols without the need for prefunctionalization.
Compared with reactions of unsaturated hydrocarbons with a
single reactive site such as alkynes, multiple reactive sites of
allenes complicated the chemo-, regio-, and stereoselectivity
issues. Therefore, transformations of allenes have remained
rare and more challenging. Significant progresses on catalytic
enantioselective coupling of allenes and aldehydes promoted
by Ir-based,<sup>2</sup> Ru-based,<sup>3</sup> Cu-based,<sup>4</sup> Pd-based,<sup>5</sup> and Rh-based<sup>6</sup>
catalysts have been made (Scheme 1a). Such reactions
proceeded through sequential nucleophile−metal addition to
allenes followed by enantioselective reactions of the resulting
allyl−metal species with aldehydes. Based on the reaction
mechanism, only one molecule of aldehyde was able to be

An alternative pathway for reactions of allenes and aldehydes
is oxidative cyclization. Oxidative cyclization of two π-bonds
promoted by low-valent transition metal complexes represents
a classical elementary step in organometallic chemistry.
Transition metal-catalyzed transformations through oxidative
cyclization constitute one of the most important approaches
for carbon−carbon bond-forming reactions in organic syn-
thesis. Although protocols for catalytic enantioselective
coupling of various unsaturated hydrocarbons and alde-
hydes/imines through oxidative cyclization have been
reported, only one molecule of electrophilic aldehydes/imines
could be incorporated (Scheme 1c).<sup>8</sup> In contrast to reactions
of alkynes and 1,3-dienes, we developed the only example of
cobalt-catalyzed divergent enantioselective 1:1 coupling of
allenes and aldehydes through oxidative cyclization.<sup>9</sup> For 1:2
transformations of unsaturated hydrocarbons with electro-
philes, pioneering work on cobalt-catalyzed enantioselective
sequential coupling of
-enynes with two molecules of
ethylene was described by RajanBabu and co-workers (Scheme
1d).<sup>10</sup> Subsequently, our group developed a cobalt-catalyzed
protocol for enantioselective divergent coupling of 1,3-enynes
with two molecules of acrylates.<sup>11</sup> In both cases, two carbon−
carbon bonds were formed at the alkyne moiety. Connecting
two molecules of aldehydes to unsaturated hydrocarbons and
incorporating two molecules of electrophiles onto an alkene
moiety remained unknown. We imagined that taking advantage
of our previous work on cobalt-catalyzed regiodivergent and
enantioselective coupling of 1,1-disubstituted allenes and
aldehydes,<sup>9</sup> the metallacycle (I, II, or III) containing an
allyl−cobalt unit generated from oxidative cyclization of allenes
and aldehydes might undergo allyl addition to the second
molecule of aldehyde, enabling double functionalization of the
more sterically congested alkene of the allenes (Scheme 1e).

Cascade reaction of 1,1-disubstituted allene 1a and benzalde
hyde 2a promoted by the Co complex derived from
bisphosphine 6i bearing a ferrocene skeleton delivered 1,4-
diol 3a exclusively in 55% yield with 88:12 dr and 95:5 er for
the major diastereomer, enabling simultaneous establishment
of three stereogenic centers (entry 9). Optimization of cobalt
salts revealed that only cobalt halides could promote the
reaction, albeit with erosion of enantioselectivity (entries 10
and 11). Increasing the amount of Zn led to an improvement
in eficiency (entries 12 and 13). An increased reaction
temperature resulted in a decrease in diastereoselectivity,
whereas performing the reaction at
2 2 ~ ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }
furnished 1,4-diol 3a
in 65% yield with 89:11 dr and 97:3 er for the major
diastereomer (entries 14−16). Alteration of the amount of
water suggested that the highest eficiency was obtained with
1.5 equiv of water (entries 17−19). A slight increase in the
catalyst loading to 6.0 mol % CoI and 7.2 mol % 6i improved
the eficiency, whereas further increasing the amount of the
catalyst did not provide a better yield (entry 20).
With the optimal conditions in hand, we investigated the
scope of allenes (Scheme 2). 1,1-Disubstituted allenes bearing
electron-deficient (3b−d and 3l), electron-rich (3g−k, 3n, and
3o), halogenated (3d−f, 3l, and 3m), and sterically congested
(3g and 3o) aryl groups underwent the cascade 1:2 reductive
coupling, afording the enantioenriched 1,4-diols in 37−68%
yields with 76:24−92:8 dr and 94:6−98:2 er for the major
diastereomer. Pyridyl-substituted allene was well tolerated
(3p). Functional groups such as ester (3c) and amine (3h) are
compatible with the reaction conditions. Reaction of silyl-
substituted allene delivered 1,4-diol 3q in 58% yield with >98:2
dr albeit 73:27 er for the major diastereomer. Allenes
substituted with two alkyl groups could be transformed into
the desired 1,4-diols (3r−t) in 31−63% yields with 86:14 to
>98:2 dr and 83:17−93:7 er for the major diastereomer.
Bisphosphine 6f was optimal for the transformation of
commercially available dimethyl-substituted allene without
the need for the addition of water, furnishing 1,4-diol 3u in
77% yield with >98:2 dr and 89:11 er. It should be mentioned
that in some cases (3c, 3d, 3h, 3i, and 3o), diastereomers
could be separated by silica gel chromatography. Monosub-
stituted allenes could not be converted into the desired
products. Oligomerization of allenes occurred preferentially.
We next explored the scope of the aldehydes (Scheme 3).
Only aryl aldehydes could participate in the cascade reaction.
Aliphatic aldehydes were unreactive under the reaction
conditions. A variety of aldehydes containing electron-rich
(7a, 7d, 7e, and 7h−m), electron-deficient (7c and 7g),
halogenated (7c, 7g, 7l, and 7m), and sterically congested (7a
and 7i−m) aryl groups could be converted into the desired
1,4-diols in 34−77% yields with 83:17−92:8 dr and 92:8−98:2
er for the major diastereomer. Functional groups such as silyl
(7b), thiol ether (7e), and styrene (7f) are quite compatible.
Although sizable 3,4-disubstituted benzaldehydes were able to
be transformed into the desired 1,4-diols (7j−m), aryl
aldehydes bearing a substituent at position 2 were unreactive.
Reactions of heteroaryl aldehydes (7n and 7o) delivered the
enantioenriched 1,4-diols in 37−48% yields with 81:19−86:14
dr and 91:9−97:3 er for the major diastereomer.

We next explored the scope of the aldehydes (Scheme 3).
Only aryl aldehydes could participate in the cascade reaction.
Aliphatic aldehydes were unreactive under the reaction
conditions. A variety of aldehydes containing electron-rich
(7a, 7d, 7e, and 7h−m), electron-deficient (7c and 7g),
halogenated (7c, 7g, 7l, and 7m), and sterically congested (7a
and 7i−m) aryl groups could be converted into the desired
1,4-diols in 34−77% yields with 83:17−92:8 dr and 92:8−98:2
er for the major diastereomer. Functional groups such as silyl
(7b), thiol ether (7e), and styrene (7f) are quite compatible.
Although sizable 3,4-disubstituted benzaldehydes were able to
be transformed into the desired 1,4-diols (7j−m), aryl
aldehydes bearing a substituent at position 2 were unreactive.
Reactions of heteroaryl aldehydes (7n and 7o) delivered the
enantioenriched 1,4-diols in 37−48% yields with 81:19−86:14
dr and 91:9−97:3 er for the major diastereomer.
Scheme 5. Mechanistic Studies
The cascade reaction can be performed on a gram scale
(Scheme 4a). Transformation of 1,1-disubstituted allene 1b
(1.037 g) with benzaldehyde 2a (2.228 g) promoted by the Co
complex derived from 6i furnished 1,4-diol 3d (1.580 g) in
64% yield with 93:7 dr and 95:5 er. Directed epoxidation of
the 1,1-disubstituted alkene moiety induced by VO(acac)
enabled highly diastereoselective construction of other stereo-
genic centers in 95% yields (Scheme 4b).<sup>13</sup> Cyclization of 1,4-
diol 3d aforded P-stereogenic phosphoramidites 9 and 11 in
64% and 43% yields with 86:14 and 82:18 dr, respectively
(Scheme 4c,d).<sup>14,15</sup> In particular, phosphoramidite 11 could be
isolated with 95:5 dr, showing its potential as a new class of P-
stereogenic phosphoramidite ligands.
To gain some mechanistic insight, we conducted a series of
experiments (Scheme 5). Increasing the amount of water to 10
equiv led to complete suppression of the cascade 1:2 coupling
reaction (Scheme 5a). Competitive 1:1 coupling product 4a
was formed exclusively. Such a result indicated that 3a and 4a
were generated via the same metallacycle intermediate. The
stereochemical control of the oxidative cyclization was not
exclusive, causing diastereomers after the second aldehyde
addition. Removal of water from the reaction conditions
resulted in a significant decrease in the reaction eficiency,
suggesting that water was crucial for the second aldehyde
addition and/or catalyst turnover (Scheme 5b). Trans-
formation of allene 1a in the absence of aldehyde 2a provided
a complex mixture of self-oligomerization products, implying
that the catalyst accurately controlled the chemoselectivity of
the initial oxidative cyclization process (Scheme 5c). Parallel
isotope kinetic experiments illustrated that cleavage of the O−
H bond of water might be the rate-determining step (Scheme
Based on all of the experimental observations and literature
precedents, we propose the possible catalytic cycle (Scheme
5e). Oxidative cyclization of allene 1a and benzaldehyde 2a
promoted by Co(I) complex II in situ generated from Co(II)
precursor I aforded Co(III) metallacycle III bearing an allyl−
Co(III) moiety, which was able to undergo allyl isomerization
via π-allyl−Co(III) intermediate IV to aford more stable
allyl−Co(III) complex V containing a tetrasubstituted alkene.
The 1,3-allylic strain in VI led to a more favorable formation of
intermediate V. One-electron reduction of Co(III) metalla-
cycle V to Co(II) species VII followed by allyl addition to
benzaldehyde 2a and subsequent protonation/exchange with a
Zn salt released product 3a. The second allyl addition might be
accelerated by detaching the OH group and assisted by Zn salt
and water (VII → VIII). Reduction of the Co(II) species with
Zn regenerated the catalyst.
In conclusion, we have disclosed an unprecedented protocol
for chemo-, regio-, diastereo-, and enantioselective cascade
coupling of 1,1-disubstituted allenes and aldehydes promoted
by a Co complex derived from a commercially available
bisphosphine ligand, afording a broad scope of enantioen-
riched 1,4-diols that are otherwise dificult to access and
enabling simultaneous construction of three stereogenic
centers. The synthetic utility was demonstrated by function-
alization of the products, delivering densely functionalized 1,4-
diols and P-stereogenic phosphoramidites. Mechanistic studies
revealed a novel cascade reaction pathway for cobalt catalysis.
Such discoveries unveiled new opportunities for designing new
cobalt-catalyzed enantioselective reactions and pushing for-
ward the development of organocobalt chemistry. Further
investigations of other cobalt-catalyzed enantioselective
cascade transformations are underway.
